scams.name: Acapulco Guerrero-State Safety Context & 'Authentic Local Tour' Risk
scams.description: Acapulco is in Guerrero state — under US State Department Level 4 'Do Not Travel' advisory due to cartel violence — and 2025 tourism has only partially recovered from Hurricane Otis (Cat 5, October 2023) which devastated the city. Community reports from 2025 consistently flag the US State Department Level 4 advisory, and travelers and Guerrero residents both express ongoing safety concerns in 2025 threads covering the broader Mexico safety baseline. The 2025 reality: (a) Acapulco's Diamante (south, newer) and Costera (Acapulco Bay strip) tourist zones are STATISTICALLY safer than the broader city — heavy police presence, well-patrolled, cruise-port active; (b) outer Acapulco neighbourhoods (Renacimiento, Zapata, Acapulco Tradicional north) have elevated cartel-related risk and are NOT recommended for tourist visits; (c) Mexico City-Acapulco highway (the 'Autopista del Sol') has documented cartel checkpoints — NOT recommended as tourist drive; fly instead; (d) Taxco day-trip from Acapulco (4-hour drive each way) crosses risky rural Guerrero — go to Taxco from Mexico City instead; (e) 'authentic local Guerrero tour' offers via Instagram/WhatsApp targeting tourists for 'rural village experience' carry real cartel-zone risk; (f) Pie de la Cuesta / Coyuca lagoon day-trip is generally safe via licensed operator but risky via informal 'beach taxi' guide. For older travellers: (1) IF visiting Acapulco, stay in Diamante or Costera zones — avoid outer neighbourhoods; (2) FLY between Mexico City and Acapulco — DO NOT drive the Autopista del Sol as a tourist; one-hour Aeromexico/VivaAerobus flights are MX$1,800-3,500; (3) for Taxco visit, go from Mexico City (3-hour drive on safer highways), NOT Acapulco; (4) REFUSE every 'authentic Guerrero village tour' Instagram/WhatsApp invitation; (5) check US State Department advisory before booking (travel.state.gov/Acapulco) — Level 4 is the highest US warning tier; (6) travel insurance with full evacuation coverage is essential for Guerrero; (7) save US Embassy 24-hr emergency +52 55 8526 2561; Mexican tourist police 911 (English available); (8) Hurricane Otis recovery context: many small businesses still rebuilding 2025 — verify hotel/restaurant operating status BEFORE booking via direct phone call.
scams.avoidance: Stay in Diamante or Costera tourist zones only FLY Mexico City-Acapulco (Aeromexico/VivaAerobus MX$1,800-3,500) Visit Taxco from Mexico City (3-hour drive), NOT from Acapulco REFUSE every 'authentic Guerrero village' tour invitation Check travel.state.gov advisory; insurance with evacuation; US Embassy +52 55 8526 2561
scams.location: Outside Acapulco Diamante / Costera tourist zones, rural Guerrero day-trip routes (Taxco, Pie de la Cuesta back-roads), Mexico City-Acapulco highway, 'authentic local' tour invitations

scams.name: Acapulco Airport (ACA) & Cruise-Port Taxi Mafia Overcharge
scams.description: Acapulco International Airport (ACA) and the cruise port have a documented 2025 taxi-overcharge ecosystem amplified by post-Hurricane Otis tourism scarcity (drivers hungry for fares). 2025 community reports cover the broader Acapulco-arrival landscape and safety context. Legitimate fares: ACA airport to Costera (15 km, 25 min) via official Transporte Terrestre prepaid MX$450-600; via Uber MX$300-450 (Uber works in Acapulco but supply is THIN — wait 10-20 min); to Diamante (12 km, 20 min) MX$350-500. Cruise pier to Costera MX$200-300 via taxi; to La Quebrada cliff divers MX$300-400. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) ACA arrivals-kerb kiosks quoting MX$1,200-2,500 for Costera transfer (2-5x real); (b) 'VIP private driver' at MX$3,500 for standard sedan; (c) 'security escort fee MX$300' added after the trip (no such legitimate fee); (d) Uber driver cancelling and re-quoting cash — same pattern as CDMX/Mazatlán; (e) cruise-pier 'authorised taxi' US$50-80 for trip that's MX$200-300 metered; (f) 'combined airport + cliff divers + sunset US$250 per person' bundle marked up 4x DIY cost; (g) 'Diamante private transfer with security US$200' upsells exploiting safety fears; (h) hotel concierge kickback directing to 'recommended driver' at 2x Uber rate. Community reports from 2025 confirm that hotel-arranged 'travel agency' tours are essentially always scam operations. For older travellers: (1) book Uber on airport Wi-Fi after luggage — typical ACA-Costera MX$300-450 (Uber works, 10-20 min wait); (2) alternatively official Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth inside arrivals MX$450-600 (legitimate flat-rate); (3) IGNORE every arrivals-kerb kiosk quoting MX$1,200+; (4) hotel airport pickup is the safest option — most Costera/Diamante hotels include free transfer with advance booking; (5) at cruise pier, use the OFFICIAL SECTUR taxi stand (rate posted) MX$200-300 to Costera; refuse 'private US$50' offers; (6) REFUSE 'security escort fee' and 'safety surcharge' demands — illegitimate; (7) for return to ACA, pre-book Uber or Transporte Terrestre night before; (8) save Acapulco Tourist Police +52 744 484 4583 (English available) and US Embassy +52 55 8526 2561.
scams.avoidance: Book Uber on airport Wi-Fi: ACA-Costera MX$300-450 (10-20 min wait) Or Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth MX$450-600 Use hotel free airport pickup (most include with advance booking) Cruise pier: official SECTUR taxi MX$200-300 to Costera Tourist Police +52 744 484 4583; US Embassy +52 55 8526 2561
scams.location: Acapulco International Airport (ACA) arrivals, Acapulco cruise port, Costera Miguel Alemán hotel drop-offs, Diamante resort transfer routes

scams.name: La Quebrada Cliff Divers 'Premium View' & Photo Tout Scam
scams.description: Acapulco's La Quebrada cliff divers (clavadistas) — performing 35-meter dives into a narrow ocean inlet five times daily — is the city's iconic free public spectacle. The 2025 tout ecosystem around the show exploits tourists unfamiliar with the legitimate viewing options. Community reports from 2025 flag broader Acapulco tourism scams, and 2024 cruise-passenger reports cover Quebrada visits. Legitimate options: (a) FREE viewing from the public plaza (Mirador de la Quebrada) — best for the noon, 1 PM, and 7:30 PM dives; (b) El Mirador Hotel 'Coyuca 22' restaurant or 'La Perla' bar — order a drink/meal (MX$200-500) and watch from the terrace with the best angle; (c) 'official' clavadistas plaza ticket MX$50-80 for guaranteed seating during the 9:30 PM torch dive (the most spectacular). The total visit cost should be MX$50-200 per person. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) 'premium VIP viewing area MX$500 per person' touts at the plaza approach — no such VIP area exists at the public viewpoint; (b) 'photographer with telephoto for the dive' service quoting MX$300-800 then delivering blurry phone-photo (real professional photos are sold by the divers' association at MX$100); (c) 'private terrace reservation US$100 per person' at La Perla bar (a drink + view is MX$200 at the bar); (d) 'cliff diver meet & greet MX$400' (divers post-show take free tips MX$30-50 — no formal 'meet & greet' fee exists); (e) 'sunset cliff dive special show MX$1,000' — the 7:30 PM dive is one of the regular five daily, free to view from plaza; (f) bundled cruise-day 'Quebrada VIP + hotel transfer US$120' marking up MX$300 actual cost. For older travellers: (1) for the 7:30 PM or 9:30 PM dive, arrive 30-45 min early to get a good spot at the public plaza viewpoint (FREE); (2) for guaranteed seating, the 9:30 PM torch dive plaza ticket is MX$50-80 (sold at the gate); (3) for the BEST view, order a drink at La Perla bar (Hotel El Mirador) — MX$200 buys you a margarita and the terrace view; (4) REFUSE every 'VIP viewing area MX$500', 'private photographer MX$300', 'meet & greet MX$400' offer — none is legitimate; (5) tip individual divers post-show MX$30-50 if you want to thank them; (6) cliff-diver photographs available at the divers' association booth MX$80-100; (7) the divers' show times (varies seasonally): 1 PM, 7:30 PM, 8:30 PM, 9:30 PM, 10:30 PM — verify on quebradacliffsdivers.com; (8) Quebrada is in Old Acapulco — well-policed during show hours but take Uber back to hotel after dark.
scams.avoidance: Arrive 30-45 min early at FREE public plaza for 7:30/9:30 PM dive Or 9:30 PM torch dive plaza ticket MX$50-80 at gate for guaranteed seat Best view: order MX$200 margarita at La Perla bar (Hotel El Mirador) REFUSE 'VIP viewing', 'private photographer', 'meet & greet' upsells Tip divers post-show MX$30-50; photos at association booth MX$80-100
scams.location: La Quebrada cliff diver platform, El Mirador Hotel observation terrace, photo-tout zone at Quebrada plaza approach, sunset show venues

scams.name: Acapulco Diamante Resort Timeshare & 'Hurricane-Recovery' Pressure Sale
scams.description: Acapulco's Diamante and Costera resort sectors host a 2025 timeshare-presentation ecosystem with a unique post-Hurricane-Otis 'rebuilding investment' angle. Community reports from 2025 flag hotel-pitch scams, and the US State Department Level 4 advisory context makes 'investment in Acapulco' pitches especially risky. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Diamante resort welcome desks (Princess Mundo Imperial, Vidanta Acapulco) offering 'free breakfast + US$200 credit + Diamante access' for '90-min preview'; (b) 'Acapulco rebuilding investment opportunity US$25,000+' pitched as patriotic post-Otis recovery (high-risk speculative); (c) 'fractional ownership rental yield 8-12% guaranteed' — no rental yield can be guaranteed in a USDOS Level 4 destination; (d) high-pressure 3-5 hour presentations with closer escalation; (e) 'snowbird membership US$15,000-30,000' targeting US/Canadian retirees; (f) 'cancellation fee US$500' to exit early; (g) 'celebrity endorser' name-drop tactics (Hurricane Otis recovery features prominently in pitches); (h) 'Mexican real estate fideicomiso required US$5,000 admin fee' — fideicomiso IS the legal structure for foreigner property in Mexico's restricted coastal zone, but admin fees are normally MX$10,000-25,000 (US$600-1,500), not US$5,000. For older travellers: (1) JUST SAY NO at Diamante / Costera resort welcome desks — 'free breakfast + credit' offers are timeshare pitches in disguise; (2) IF attending, set 90-min HARD STOP and stand to leave regardless of tactics; (3) NEVER authorise credit-card 'holds' or 'deposits' during presentation; (4) Mexican 5-business-day cooling-off period is LAW — file PROFECO (profeco.gob.mx) + registered mail to property's legal department within window if you signed; (5) CRITICAL: 'Acapulco rebuilding investment' is high-risk speculative — Hurricane Otis (Cat 5, October 2023) destroyed huge infrastructure; recovery is ongoing; cartel-violence safety overlay makes Acapulco real estate a poor investment for casual buyers; (6) for genuine Mexican property, consult a LICENSED Mexican real-estate attorney (NOT the resort's 'legal counsel') with verifiable Notario Público; (7) REFUSE any 'fideicomiso admin US$5,000' — real range is US$600-1,500; (8) US Consulate Acapulco closed 2024 — nearest US Consulate is Mexico City Embassy +52 55 8526 2561; (9) community reports from 2025 confirm that 'travel agencies' approaching at hotel are essentially always timeshare-pitch organizations.
scams.avoidance: JUST SAY NO at Diamante / Costera resort welcome desks If attending, 90-min hard stop; stand and walk out regardless of tactics NEVER authorise credit-card 'holds' or 'deposits' Mexican 5-day cooling-off: file PROFECO if signed For property, consult licensed Mexican real-estate attorney; refuse 'investment' speculation
scams.location: Acapulco Diamante resort welcome desks (Mundo Imperial, Princess Mundo Imperial, Vidanta), Costera resort timeshare booths, post-Otis 'rebuilding investment' pitches

scams.name: Acapulco Costera Restaurant Tourist-Menu & 'Mariscos Market Price' Padding
scams.description: Acapulco's Costera Miguel Alemán beachfront restaurant strip and Diamante mall dining hosts a 2025 tourist-menu bill-padding ecosystem common to Mexican beach destinations. Community reports from 2025 cover the broader Acapulco scam landscape, and 2024 cruise-day reports document dining patterns. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Costera beachfront restaurants with USD-only menus at 2-3x local prices (huachinango fish dish US$30+ vs MX$200-300 at working-class spots); (b) 'mariscos market price' verbal quotes for shrimp/lobster/fish without weight × price/kg disclosed — bills run MX$1,500-3,500; (c) 'gratuity 18%' pre-added + tip line (double-tipping); (d) 'credit-card processing 10-15%' announced at bill; (e) 'complimentary chips/guacamole' arriving as MX$280 line item; (f) 'fresh coconut water US$8' from beach-vendor at restaurant when fair MX$30-50; (g) USD-priced menus padding 10-15% exchange; (h) 'live mariachi service charge MX$100/person' added unannounced; (i) 'special seafood platter market price' that's whatever they decide to charge; (j) Acapulco Old-town zócalo restaurants charging Diamante prices to cruise tourists. For older travellers: (1) eat at AUTHENTIC Acapulco spots: La Cabaña de Caleta (Caleta beach, Mexican seafood, Google 4.6+, MX$250-450), El Cabrito (Costera, traditional Mexican, MX$200-400), 100% Natural (Costera multi-locations, healthier MX$150-300), Becco al Mare (Costera Italian, transparent MX$300-500 per person); (2) for shrimp/seafood, agree weight × price/kg IN WRITING before cooking — fair shrimp MX$400-600/kg, lobster MX$1,000-1,500/kg, fish MX$200-400/kg depending on type; (3) INSPECT bill — refuse 'gratuity 18% + tip' double-dipping; confirm card surcharge 0-3% BEFORE ordering; (4) request MX$ bill (not USD); (5) REFUSE uninvited 'complimentary' appetizers (always charged); (6) for budget eats, Mercado Central de Acapulco (Old Acapulco) has authentic seafood at MX$80-150 per meal; (7) refuse 'live mariachi service charge' — if you want music, agree per-song MX$100-200 with the musicians directly; (8) coconut water from beach vendor: MX$30-50 fair (NEVER US$8 in MX$ pesos).
scams.avoidance: Authentic: La Cabaña de Caleta, El Cabrito, 100% Natural, Becco al Mare Seafood: weight × price/kg IN WRITING; fair shrimp MX$400-600/kg Inspect bill; refuse double-tipping; card 0-3% Mercado Central de Acapulco for budget MX$80-150 Mariachi: agree per-song MX$100-200 with musicians directly
scams.location: Costera Miguel Alemán beachfront restaurants, Acapulco Diamante mall dining, Old Acapulco zócalo perimeter, cruise-day tourist-menu spots

scams.name: Acapulco Beach Vendor & 'Free Massage' Aggressive Pressure Scam
scams.description: Acapulco's public beaches host an active 2025 vendor culture with aggressive pressure tactics. Community reports from 2025 cover the broader pitch-pressure context, and cruise-day and visit reports confirm the same landscape. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) beach vendors walking up every 30-60 seconds offering sarongs, jewelry, hair-braids, henna tattoos, parasailing, jet-ski, banana-boat — aggressive 'special price my friend' opening; (b) 'free henna tattoo' that becomes MX$400 when you try to leave; (c) 'massage on the beach MX$300 for 60 min' becoming MX$1,200 'extended deluxe' bill; (d) 'parasail US$80' (legitimate operators MX$700-900 = US$40-50 with comparison-shopping); (e) 'banana-boat ride MX$500 per person' (real MX$200-300); (f) 'photo with iguana / parrot / macaw MX$300-500' (wildlife welfare concern + mass-overcharged); (g) 'beach chair rental US$25' at FREE public sand; (h) 'fresh fruit cup MX$80' (real MX$25-40 from licensed vendors); (i) 'mariachi serenade MX$500 for 3 songs' that becomes MX$1,500 with 'tip expected'; (j) 'safety surveillance fee US$10/day' from fake 'beach security' (no such fee). For older travellers: (1) firm 'no gracias' and keep walking; don't stop, smile, or engage beach vendors; (2) all Mexican beaches are PUBLIC federal property — no entrance fee, no chair-rental obligation, no 'safety fee'; legitimate beach clubs have posted price boards; (3) REFUSE every 'free' offer — henna, massage, photos, fruit, drinks; (4) for parasail, jet-ski, banana-boat, COMPARISON-SHOP 3+ operators on the beach; legitimate rates: parasail MX$600-900 (10-15 min), jet-ski MX$700-1,000 (30 min), banana-boat MX$200-300 per person; (5) for massage, book at hotel spa or Spa Diamante / Spa Pacha at MX$800-1,500 for proper 60-90 min; (6) REFUSE 'photo with exotic animal' — wildlife-welfare violation + 100% scam; (7) take photos yourself with phone timer; never hand phone to 'photographer' tout; (8) for fresh fruit, buy at Mercado Central or licensed beach vendor with posted prices MX$25-40 per cup; (9) refuse 'beach safety fee' — illegitimate; (10) Caleta and Caletilla (Old Acapulco) are calmer than Costera Hornos for older travellers; pier-shuttle to Roqueta Island is MX$70 round-trip if you want a beach day-trip from Old Acapulco.
scams.avoidance: Firm 'no gracias' and keep walking; no engagement Beaches are PUBLIC — no entry fee, no chair-rental obligation Comparison-shop 3+ operators: parasail MX$600-900, jet-ski MX$700-1,000 Massage at hotel spa or Spa Diamante MX$800-1,500 (not beach) REFUSE 'exotic animal photos'; refuse 'beach safety fee' demands
scams.location: Playa Caleta + Caletilla (Old Acapulco beaches), Playa Hornos / Playa Hornitos Costera, Playa Diamante public stretches, Playa Pie de la Cuesta lagoon side
